newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees at least two percent growth in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees at least two percent growth in 1998.

text.p: A new seven-point Russian government plan to stimulate the economy announced on Monday predicted economic growth would be at least two percent in 1998 but made no mention of general economic growth this year.

"Already this year a real climb in domestic industrial output will begin, and in 1998 the pace of economic growth will be no less than two percent," Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said in a statement on the plan dated May 19.
His remarks were the latest sign that the authorities are slipping on their predictions for the timetable for economic recovery.
The 1997 budget anticipates that gross domestic product (GDP), the widest indicator of a country's economic growth, would increase two percent this year.
Late last month First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said Russia could see 0.5 to 2.5 percent growth this year.

Russian industrial production was up 0.4 percent in March on a year ago, while GDP was 0.2 percent higher in the first quarter of the year than in the same period in 1996, the State Statistics Committee has said.
